_comment: needs human review before production deployment. Conservative emergency procedures for Himalayan and Northeast terrain.

scenarios.title: Trapped by Landslide
scenarios.summary: Cut off by active slope failure or debris flow across mountain corridor.
steps: Move away from the slide path immediately to stable bedrock ground or solid ridges.
Watch uphill for secondary rockfalls, rolling boulders, and uprooted trees; never cross fresh active debris.
If inside a vehicle, unbuckle and prepare to exit if safe solid ground is accessible; otherwise brace low against small stones.
Stay visible: deploy bright clothing, emergency whistle (3 sharp blasts), or flashing headlamp.
Conserve phone battery: switch to Low Power mode, disable background apps, and keep GPS on.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 immediately if someone is buried, trapped in a vehicle, or debris flow is advancing toward your shelter point.
safeActions: Seek higher bedrock ground immediately
Never attempt to drive across active slide debris
Signal with whistle (3 blasts per minute)

scenarios.title: Road Blocked
scenarios.summary: Roadway obstructed by boulder, tree fall, or earth slip ahead.
steps: Stop at least 50 meters before the hazard zone; park away from steep roadside cliff cuttings.
Turn on hazard blinkers to alert vehicles approaching behind you around blind mountain curves.
Do not attempt to drive through debris or walk across loose uncompacted scree.
Check RouteX for alternative routes or turn back to the nearest safe inhabited settlement.
Report the obstruction on RouteX when signal is available so other travelers avoid this segment.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 or local traffic helpline if the road collapse isolates vehicles with vulnerable passengers or medical needs.
safeActions: Turn around to the nearest safe town or shelter
Avoid parking beneath sheer rock overhangs
Log a community hazard report

scenarios.title: Injured / Medical Emergency
scenarios.summary: Physical injury, hypothermia, fracture, or altitude illness on mountain route.
steps: Halt all movement and evaluate airway, breathing, and severe external bleeding.
Control bleeding with direct firm pressure using clean dressing; wrap in emergency thermal blanket.
Do not move a person with suspected spine, neck, or pelvic trauma unless in immediate rockfall danger.
Record exact GPS coordinates, altitude, and timestamps of symptom progression.
Transmit RouteX SOS emergency dispatch with coordinates and condition summary.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 immediately for any head trauma, compound fracture, uncontrollable bleeding, or severe hypothermia.
safeActions: Apply emergency first aid and direct pressure
Protect against cold ground using sleeping pad or dry packs
Broadcast SOS coordinates to emergency contacts

scenarios.title: Lost on Trail
scenarios.summary: Disoriented, fogged in, or separated from marked mountain trail.
steps: S.T.O.P: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan. Do not panic or rush blindly through rough terrain.
Check compass orientation and last confirmed trail cairn before moving downhill into unknown gullies.
Never descend into steep river gorges or waterfalls where vertical rock walls trap hikers.
Stay on open ridge lines or distinct clearings where search visibility and cellular signal are highest.
If darkness approaches, bivvy in place against wind; do not attempt nocturnal descent.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 or NDMA 1078 if darkness is falling, sub-zero temperatures threaten, or you lack overnight bivvy gear.
safeActions: Stay high on visible ridgelines
Avoid wet stream beds and slippery ravines
Signal 3 loud whistle blasts periodically

scenarios.title: Flood / Rising Water
scenarios.summary: Flash flood, sudden glacial outburst, or bursting stream across roadway.
steps: Climb to high ground immediately away from riverbeds, seasonal nullahs, and low culverts.
Never attempt to drive or walk through flowing mountain water deeper than ankle height.
Be alert for flash flood surges upstream caused by temporary landslide dam breaches.
Move upstream and away from vertical embankments that can undercut and collapse into the torrent.
Wait out the crest on solid high ground; mountain runoff surges typically recede after storm peak.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 if water levels are rising around stranded vehicles or occupants are cut off from high ground.
safeActions: Evacuate perpendicular to stream flow up hillside
Do not drive into submerged roadway dips
Stay clear of undercut river banks

scenarios.title: Earthquake
scenarios.summary: Ground shaking, structural tremors, and subsequent seismic rockfalls.
steps: Drop, Cover, and Hold On. Protect head and neck with your arms or heavy pack.
If outdoors in mountain terrain, move clear of steep cliffs, loose scree fields, and high power lines.
Anticipate secondary landslides and aftershocks within the next 24 to 72 hours.
Turn off vehicle engine and park away from bridges, overpasses, and loose retaining walls.
Inspect travel companions for injuries before moving carefully to open flat clearings.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 or NDMA 1078 if structural collapse, road severance, or trapped persons require immediate rescue teams.
safeActions: Protect head and vital organs
Anticipate aftershocks on unstable slopes
Assemble in open meadows or wide clearings

scenarios.title: Heavy Rain on Mountain Road
scenarios.summary: Torrential downpours saturating slope layers and reducing tire traction.
steps: Reduce speed immediately to 20-30 km/h; maintain triple standard braking distance.
Turn on low-beam headlights and defroster; watch for muddy runoff chutes washing across turns.
Pull into the next designated safe haven, fuel station, or hotel until rainfall rates decline.
Do not stop in known landslide zones or right next to steep excavated earth cuts.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 if visibility drops to zero with stranded traffic or mud deposits blocking both lanes.
safeActions: Drive at low speeds with lights on
Seek verified shelter in nearest town
Avoid stopping under unstable rock cuts

scenarios.title: No Cellular Signal
scenarios.summary: Total cellular dead zone in deep Himalayan valley or high pass.
steps: Rely on RouteX downloaded offline PMTiles maps and cached route directions.
Move towards higher ridge points or roadside ITBP/BRO military outposts for emergency radio relay.
Leave visible travel markers or notes on parked vehicle stating your destination and departure time.
Conserve battery by toggling Airplane Mode while keeping GPS location services active.
scenarios.whenToCall112: When network returns or at nearest police checkpost (ITBP/BRO), report your status and time of passage.
safeActions: Use downloaded offline maps
Move to higher terrain for line-of-sight signal
Save battery with Airplane Mode

scenarios.title: Stranded at Night
scenarios.summary: Nightfall in mountain sector with low temperatures and limited road visibility.
steps: Pull off the main roadway into a wide turnout, verified hotel parking, or well-lit petrol pump.
Lock vehicle doors, crack one window 5 mm for ventilation if running heater periodically.
Never run engine continuously while sleeping due to deadly carbon monoxide accumulation.
Use layers, sleeping bags, and thermal emergency blankets to preserve body core heat.
Wait for morning daylight before attempting unfamiliar mountain navigation.
scenarios.whenToCall112: Call 112 if freezing temperatures pose imminent hypothermia risk or vehicle battery is depleted.
safeActions: Shelter in vehicle or registered stay
Ventilate if operating vehicle engine
Wait for daylight before driving
